doc.name: A — mechanical keyboard catalogue, miniature diorama, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: 65 percent hot-swap keyboard
Category: mechanical keyboard
Shot programme: miniature diorama
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the still-life director on a commercial mechanical keyboard shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the in-hand scale in a miniature diorama treatment.

SUBJECT. A 65 percent hot-swap keyboard. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Held in a hand that provides scale, hand cropped at the wrist. Shoot on an 85mm short telephoto at f/16, framing for a tight crop that breaks the subject at the frame edge.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with a beauty dish above the lens axis with a silver reflector under the chin. Stage the product on or against wet terrazzo, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward near-monochrome with a single accent hue allowed to stay saturated. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

COLOUR. Grade toward a cinematic grade with a warm key and green-leaning ambient shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Reply with a single continuous prompt paragraph. Never explain, never bullet, never wrap it in markdown fences.
